name: session_threads
title: How transport-v2 work is scheduled
summary: Sessions and relay streams each keep their handlers on a strand. One Asio event loop dispatches those handlers, and a small pool of worker threads runs the loop.
comment: Thread defaults come from src/server/cli/entry.cpp and src/client/cli/commands/io_runtime.cpp. Update the note when either changes.

nodes.title: SESSION
nodes.note: Each session queues its network and timer handlers on its own strand, so its steps never overlap or run out of order, even with several threads.

nodes.title: RELAY STREAM
nodes.note: On the client, each relay stream is serialized on one strand as well.

nodes.title: EVENT LOOP
nodes.note: Sockets and timers complete here. A handler starts a read or write and returns at once, and the loop runs the next handler when data is ready.

nodes.title: WORKER THREADS
nodes.note: Several threads run the same loop. yumed defaults to the hardware thread count and the client to at most four. A handler exception is contained so one peer cannot abort the process.
